s.g: to place in (someone's) service; to make serve; to cause to attend

s.d: literally: to fill (someone's) face with shame; hence: = causative action by which deities cause humans to be deeply ashamed in such a way that it shows on their faces
literally: to see (someone's) face; hence: = state in which humans are in the close presence of someone of a higher social status, such as a ruler, or even God himself
s.g: to see (someone's) face > to be in (someone's) presence

s.d: literally: to see (someone's) face; hence: = state in which humans are in the close presence of someone of a higher social status, such as a ruler, or even God himself
s.g: to see (someone's) face > to be in (someone's) presence

s.d: literally: to place (one's) face (in a certain direction); hence: = action by which humans turn their face in a certain direction
literally: to turn (someone else's) face (in a certain direction); hence: causative action by which humans cause animals to look into a certain direction
s.g: to turn (someone's) face (in a certain direction)

s.d: literally: to place (one's) face (in a certain direction); hence: = action by which humans or deities direct their attention to a group of (other) humans, either with positive or negative intentions
literally: to make (one's) face stand firm; hence: = action by which humans keep the expression on their face unchanged for some time
literally: to turn (one's) face; hence: = action by which humans turn their face in a certain direction
s.g: to cause to turn around; to roll

s.d: literally: to make (something) happen before (someone's) face; hence: = causative action by which a deity causes something to happen for the benefit of someone else
literally: to come before (someone's) face; hence: = process by which deities come to an conclusion as to how they are going to achieve a particular purpose
literally: face; hence: = state in which humans or deities have a strong opinion about something
literally: to set (one's) face (to do something); hence: = action by which humans exercise their minds to determine what will happen or what they will do
literally: to put before (one's) face; hence: = action by which humans decide that something is of significant importance for them and needs to be dealt with
literally: to cover (someone's) face; hence: = causative action by which deities make it impossible for humans to see certain things
s.g: to cover (someone's) face > to make (someone) blind

s.d: literally: to grind (someone's) face; hence: = causative action by which humans cause other humans to suffer harm and humiliation, ◄ which feels as if one's face has been has been crushed with a millstone
literally: to harden (one's own) face; hence: = action by which humans show themselves unwilling to listen to reason and do what is right

literally: to hide (one's) face (from someone); hence: = action by which a deity does not engage with people, and does not intervene neither in their favor nor to punish, ◄ as if he were enable to see them
literally: to arise before (someone); hence: = action by which humans reject the authority of a ruler to which they had formerly been subjected
literally: to weaken someone's face; hence: = causative action by which humans make an effort to make (other) humans or deities willing to act in their favor

literally: to lift up (someone's) face; hence: = action by which humans or deities show favor or respect to someone, ◄ as if by allowing someone who is looking down out of shame or humility to look up directly into one's face
s.g: to respect; to look upon or treat with favor; to honor

s.d: literally: hard of face; hence: = state in which humans are stubborn and unwilling to yield
literally: to turn away (someone else's) face; hence: = action by which humans or deities show their unwillingness to interact with (other) humans and honor their wishes
literally: to cast (someone) from (one's) face; hence: = action by which deities end their relationship with humans and refuse to have anything to do with them anymore
s.g: to cast from (one's) presence; to reject
